question: What is the main characteristic of passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: The nurse moves the joint while the patient remains relaxed
options.B: The patient uses their own muscle power to move the limb
options.C: The patient resists the movement applied by the nurse
options.D: The client lifts heavy weights to build muscle size

explanation: Passive exercises mean the healthcare provider supplies all the movement energy while the client's muscles stay completely inactive. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why do we perform passive range of motion exercises for a paralyzed patient?

options.A: To keep joints flexible and stop them from getting stiff
options.B: To replace the need for turning the client in bed
options.C: To help the nervous system grow new nerves
options.D: To build big muscles in the affected arms and legs

explanation: Since paralyzed muscles cannot move on their own, moving the joints passively stops them from freezing up or developing tight contractures. You've got this! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is a main goal of doing passive range of motion?
explanation: Well done! Passive movements are specifically designed to keep joints flexible when a patient cannot move themselves. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h2)

question: A patient is brought to the ward in a deep coma after a severe head injury. Which nursing action is best to prevent stiff joints?

options.A: Doing regular passive range of motion exercises
options.B: Encouraging the client to squeeze rubber balls daily
options.C: Tying all four limbs tightly to the bed rails
options.D: Putting heavy sandbags on the hands and feet

explanation: Brilliant! An unconscious client cannot move on their own, so scheduled passive range of motion keeps their joints mobile and safe. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h2)

question: When should you avoid doing passive range of motion exercises on a limb?

options.A: When the client has a fresh, unhealed bone fracture
options.B: When the ward weather is unusually warm
options.C: When the client has a mild cold
options.D: When the client feels sleepy in the afternoon

explanation: Spot on! Moving a limb with a fresh fracture disrupts bone healing and causes severe pain. Always check for fractures first! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why do you need to be very careful when doing joint exercises for an elderly client with severe osteoporosis?

options.A: Their blood circulation is already too fast
options.B: Their skin is prone to rashes easily
options.C: Their muscles will become too bulky too quickly
options.D: Their fragile bones are at high risk of breaking

explanation: Exactly! Osteoporosis makes bones weak and brittle, so gentle handling is key to preventing accidental fractures. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h3)

question: How should you support a joint while doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: Placing your hands above and below the joint
options.B: Letting the limb dangle freely without support
options.C: Holding the joint tightly right at its center point
options.D: Pulling firmly on the fingers or toes

explanation: Great job! Cradling the joint with hands positioned above and below gives solid support and protects the surrounding tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h4)

question: What should you do immediately if a patient shows signs of pain while their arm is being moved?

options.A: Continue moving faster to get past the painful spot
options.B: Ask a relative to hold the arm down so you can finish
options.C: Stop the exercise right away and check the joint
options.D: Ignore it because passive exercise always hurts

explanation: Pain is your stop sign! It tells you something is being over-stretched or injured. Always pause and assess. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h4)

question: When exercising the lower limbs, where should you place your hands to support the leg?

options.A: Under the knee and under the heel
options.B: Right on the kneecap and toes
options.C: Around the middle of the thigh bone
options.D: Firmly on the client's hip bones

explanation: Spot on! Supporting the leg at the knee and heel keeps the patient comfortable and gives you steady control. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h5)

question: What do you call bending the foot so the toes point upward toward the shin?
explanation: You got it! Dorsiflexion means pulling the ankle up so the top of the foot moves closer to the leg. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why is it important to watch the client's face during passive exercises?

options.A: To check if they are watching the television
options.B: To spot hidden pain or distress when they cannot speak well
options.C: To check how fast their hair is growing
options.D: To see if they need spectacles to read

explanation: Wonderful! Many patients can't tell you when it hurts, so a quick wince or frown on their face tells you everything you need to know. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h6)

question: After finishing passive exercises for an unconscious patient, what is the final safety step you must take?

options.A: Take the patient out of bed and put them in a chair
options.B: Leave all side rails down so family can visit easily
options.C: Leave the bed high up so it is easy to clean later
options.D: Return the bed to the lowest position and raise the side rails

explanation: Safety first! Always drop the bed low and pop the side rails up to protect your patient from falls before you walk away. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h6)

question: What details should you write down in the chart after doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: The brand name of soap used for their bath
options.B: The patient's favorite food and religious beliefs
options.C: The cost of the hospital bed and your home address
options.D: Joints exercised, how the patient tolerated it, and any unusual findings

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing notes always focus on the clinical facts: what you moved, how they reacted, and anything out of the ordinary. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h7)

question: What should you do if you notice sudden joint swelling and severe redness during an exercise session?

options.A: Cover the swollen joint with a heavy blanket and leave
options.B: Stop the exercise, report to the doctor, and document it
options.C: Massage the swollen area firmly with rubbing alcohol
options.D: Keep exercising faster to break up the swelling

explanation: Well done! Sudden swelling or redness means you need to pause right away, let the doctor know, and chart what happened. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h7)
